comparison.objective: Candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber so a carriage stops safely and repeatably; record orients two stack-nest totes and lowers each onto mating ledges without contacting the contained parts.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate tests small-tool alignment, setscrew manipulation, fine collar rotation, counterholding, bounded tightening, and iterative dynamic diagnosis. Record tests tote grasping, possible 180° reorientation, gross alignment, controlled lowering, and release. Shared pose alignment and rotation are generic primitives only.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two acceptable energized test cycles after physical unlock-adjust-lock operations, with no bottoming, hard-stop strike, overload, rebound, drift, damage, tool loss, or state writes. Record requires both released totes to rest level on ledges within height/centering tolerances for 1 s, with no nesting, excessive lowering, tilt, or parts-box displacement. Candidate lacks numeric rebound, overload, witness-torque drift, and tightening-damage thresholds, but the objectives and terminal states remain clearly unrelated.
comparison.reason: One evaluates force-response commissioning and retained adjustment of a damper; the other evaluates orientation-dependent container mating and damage-free placement. Different tote geometry alone is not the distinction—the measured physical outcomes are.
